scenes.title: Copilot Code: approve a narrow, governed preview pilot
scenes.body: Bottom line: pilot Copilot Code for one small purpose-built solution, with IT policy set first, a named owner, scoped data, a spend limit and an explicit stop-or-expand review.
scenes.narration: Bottom line: pilot Copilot Code for one small purpose-built solution, with IT policy set first, a named owner, scoped data, a spend limit and an explicit stop-or-expand review.
claims: Copilot Code is a preview build experience in the Microsoft Copilot app that requires Frontier access; the selected sources do not establish general availability.
Microsoft frames Code as a shift from files alone toward small purpose-built solutions: users describe software in natural language, see a live result, iterate, and can revert to an earlier version.
Cloud projects can publish interactive apps to Copilot Managed Runtime for people in the organization, while local projects work inside a chosen project folder.
Local mode asks for approval by default before network calls, extensions or MCP use, shell commands, or file access outside active projects; cloud mode runs in a secure isolated environment.
Copilot Code follows Microsoft 365 governance, security and compliance controls, and administrators can audit generated code, commands run, and files read or written.

For work accounts, IT must provide a Copilot license and organization-level enablement, and can configure auto-approve, execution location, GitHub connections, organizational data access and spend limits; documented defaults can change during preview.
claimSources: Introducing the new Copilot with Home, Code and Autopilot

scenes.title: 3. Configure first, then pilot narrowly
scenes.body: IT must confirm license and enablement, then set auto-approve, execution location, GitHub, organizational data and spend policies. Recommendation: one low-risk business use case, one owner, least data needed, a budget cap, and a stop-or-expand review before broader access.
